item.title: 2 Cops Placed On Leave
item.description: State police are investigating a city police officer for allegedly punching a woman while she was in handcuffs. The city's police department is also investigating a patrol supervisor for allegedly having sex while on duty on New Year's Day. The post 2 Cops Placed On Leave appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Young, Old Dems Kick Off 2026
item.description: Standing in a Crown Street bar packed with young Democratic politicos from across Connecticut, 72-year-old Gov. Ned Lamont pointed to 33-year-old East Rock/Fair Haven Alder Caroline Tanbee Smith and said, "You're happening!" While not necessarily a passing of the torch, it was recognition by the party's older generation of its burgeoning young talent. The post Young, Old Dems Kick Off 2026 appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: City Considers Taking English Station By Eminent Domain
item.description: The Elicker administration has submitted a proposal to the Board of Alders to acquire the contaminated former English Station power plant property -- if possible by negotiated sale, if necessary by eminent domain. item.title: “Archive” Landlord: We Have Too Much Parking
item.description: A Chapel Street luxury apartment complex has been leasing 23 parking spots at an off-site Ninth Square garage for over a year — which, according to the developer, no one has been using. Now, the developer is seeking zoning relief to reduce its parking requirement — and free up those parking spots for public use. The post “Archive” Landlord: We Have Too Much Parking appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Industrial Revival On Tap For Newly Sold Former Print Shop
item.description: In a few months, the former Phoenix Press building fronting Criscuolo Park will be home to both a manufacturing company and a manufacturing-training nonprofit -- infusing that corner of Fair Haven with a burst of new industrial life. item.title: Unions To Yale: Pay City $110M Per Year
item.description: At the heart of Yale's campus on Monday, several dozen people gathered for a union-led rally where they urged the university to more than quadruple its annual payments to New Haven for each of the next five years.
